title: introduce-rag-coauthoring-offline-sandbox
author: Sofia Martinez
summary: Add a compact quickstart demonstrating offline/co-authoring RAG workflows: a small sandbox that shows local index sync, CRDT-based patching for concurrent edits, and a lightweight websocket relay to simulate intermittent connectivity. The quickstart contains an authoring README, a TypeScript client that runs in the browser (with a node shim for local dev), a sample replay harness for deterministic evals, and docs site updates in the Authoring Lab section. The goal is to give developers an end-to-end example they can run locally and extend for collaborative retrieval-augmented features without requiring a managed backend. Includes tests and CI checks to verify replay determinism and index merge correctness.

detailed_description:
Context and motivation: Teams building retrieval-augmented collaborative features often need an example showing how to combine a local/offline-first authoring experience with RAG-style retrieval and a deterministic replay pipeline for tests and evals. This quickstart provides a minimal sandbox that demonstrates: 1) how to keep a small local index (chunked documents) on the client and synchronise it to a replay-friendly store; 2) a CRDT-based patch/merge primitive to reconcile concurrent edits and index diffs without losing token-level provenance; 3) a lightweight relay that simulates flaky connectivity so developers can test sync/resume behaviour; and 4) a deterministic replay harness that replays recorded events to validate retrieval stability and prompt/eval regression.

What changed: Added quickstarts/coauthoring-offline with an opinionated README and runnable steps; a browser client (example-client.ts) that can run headless with the node-shim or directly in modern browsers; lib/crdt-merge.ts implementing a small operational transform/CRDT merge util with tests; lib/indexer.ts for incremental chunking and fingerprints; replay/harness.ts to record and replay sessions; unit and smoke e2e tests under tests/; and docs/authoring-lab/coauthoring-offline.md which integrates into the docs site and includes UX guidance and suggested telemetry probes.

Testing and CI: Unit tests cover CRDT merge edge cases and index delta application; the replay harness is used in an e2e smoke job that runs with a deterministic seed to verify identical final index state across runs. CI added docs-build step and a quick smoke pipeline.

Backwards compatibility: Non-breaking. The quickstart is additive and does not change platform APIs.

How to try locally (short): 1) git clone && cd quickstarts/coauthoring-offline 2) pnpm install && pnpm dev:relay 3) open browser-client/index.html or run pnpm dev:client-headless 4) run pnpm test to validate replay smoke. Full instructions are in the README.

Related: ENG-2241 (coauthoring infra spike), PM-842 (authoring lab feature request).
